originality.rationale: Compared complete primary and nearest public published records. The binary-only cyclic inverse law and general-q one-erasure theorem do not imply a nonbinary complete read fiber spectrum; the noncyclic general-alphabet reduction is likewise a different observation model. The new nonbinary bounded-composition inverse lists, 7-level ternary family, and exact qary image size require additional normalization and counting not established in those inspected sources. General integer-circulant terminology remains residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier paper under integer circulant tomography, quotient shift equivalence or multilevel signal reconstruction terminology could imply the same formulas.
The read-erasure paper mentions noncoprime equivalence to full read fibers but does not calculate their q-ary sizes; a further unpublished or unindexed companion may exist.
Primary full-text comparison of unrelated historical venues is not exhaustive.

value.rationale: Quantifies exact reconstruction uncertainty and finite-block optimal distinguishable readouts under a natural multilevel cyclic weighted-sum observation. Distinct nonbinary inverse-list sizes include a seven-class ternary spectrum and a sharp central multinomial bottleneck absent from the binary case; exact algebraic formulas hold at every alphabet, blocklength and window length. No downstream performance or physical sequencing claims are required.
